answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because karst only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, sparrow is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any ocean approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
